([[Middletown, Delaware]]) | college = [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] (2019–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 26 | draft_team = [[Denver Nuggets]] | career_start = 2021 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team1 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | years2 = {{nbay|2022|end}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team2 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years3 = {{nbay|2024|end}}–present | team3 = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | years4 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team4 = →[[Iowa Wolves]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] ({{nbay|2021|end}}) * [[Atlantic 10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic 10 Player of the Year]] (2021) * First-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] (2021) * Atlantic 10 All-Rookie Team (2020) }} '''Nah'Shon Lee''' "'''Bones'''" '''Hyland''' (born September 14, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU Rams]] before being drafted 26th overall in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]]. ==Early life== Hyland was born in Delaware.{{cite web |last1=Reddick |first1=JJ |author1-link=JJ Redick |title=Bones Hyland Opens Up About His Life Story, Playing With Jokic, Adjusting To The NBA and More |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RWC0jnQLVOc&t=932s |website=youtube.com |language=en |format=video |date=January 3, 2023}} He started playing basketball after watching his older brother and a friend playing at the park. He was nicknamed "Bizzy Bones" or "Bones" in part due to his slender build.{{cite web |last1=Epps |first1=Wayne |title=VCU's next star, 'Bones' Hyland carries his hometown of Wilmington on his back |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/plus/vcus-next-star-bones-hyland-carries-his-hometown-of-wilmington-on-his-back/article_5208556b-e00c-5383-b9ad-cc0128b688d1.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=January 4, 2020}} Hyland attended [[St. Georges Technical High School]] in [[Middletown, Delaware]]. During his junior year, on March 25, 2018, his 11-month-old cousin and grandmother died in a [[house fire]].{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=CJ |title=A year after a tragic fire, high-major recruit Nah'Shon Hyland has his groove back |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/957786/2019/05/02/a-year-after-a-tragic-fire-high-major-recruit-nahshon-hyland-has-his-groove-back/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=May 2, 2019}} Hyland escaped by jumping from his second-floor bedroom and suffered a torn patellar tendon, sidelining him for six months.{{cite web |last1=Grube |first1=Ryan |title=After a life-altering house fire, Bones Hyland draws strength from losses |url=https://commonwealthtimes.org/2019/10/22/after-a-life-altering-house-fire-bones-hyland-draws-strength-from-losses/ |website=[[The Commonwealth Times]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=October 22, 2019}} As a senior, he averaged 26.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 3.4 steals per game, leading his team to the semifinals of the state tournament. He was named Delaware Player of the Year and earned first team All-State honors.{{cite web |last1=Myers |first1=Brad |title=St. Georges' Hyland is Player of the Year, heads All-State boys basketball team |url=https://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/15/nahshon-hyland-heads-delaware-all-state-boys-basketball-team/3177572002/ |website=[[The News Journal]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=March 15, 2019}} A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] over offers from [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]], [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]], [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]], [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]], and [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]].{{cite web |last1=Epps |first1=Wayne |title=VCU adds four-star guard Nah'Shon Hyland to 2019 recruiting class |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/schools/virginia-commonwealth-university/vcu-adds-four-star-guard-nahshon-hyland-to-2019-recruiting-class/article_c26b130a-2a0e-5a9d-a3fe-55c797c173e4.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=June 4, 2019}} ==College career== On January 18, 2020, Hyland scored a freshman season-high 21 points and five three-pointers in a 91–63 win over [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]].{{cite web |last1=Jeter |first1=Fred |title=VCU's Nah'Shon Hyland: A freshman with impact |url=http://richmondfreepress.com/news/2020/jan/31/vcus-nahshon-hyland-freshman-impact/ |website=[[Richmond Free Press]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=January 31, 2020}} As a freshman, he averaged nine points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game, earning [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] All-Rookie Team accolades. He shot 43.4 percent from three-point range and set a program freshman record with 63 three-pointers.{{cite web |title=Nah'Shon Hyland |url=https://vcuathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/nah-shon-hyland/3653 |website=Virginia Commonwealth University |access-date=December 7, 2020}} In his sophomore season debut on November 25, Hyland scored 23 points, making five three-pointers, in an 85–69 victory over [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]].{{cite web |last1=Davis |first1=Marc |title=Hyland, Williams, strong finish propel VCU past Utah State |url=https://www.nbc12.com/2020/11/26/hyland-williams-strong-finish-propel-vcu-past-utah-state/ |website=[[WWBT]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=November 26, 2020}} On December 9, he scored 30 points, shooting 7-of-12 from three-point range, in a 95–59 win over [[North Carolina A&T Aggies men's basketball|North Carolina A&T]].{{cite web |title=Hyland erupts for 30, Rams throttle Aggies |url=https://vcuathletics.com/news/2020/12/9/mens-basketball-hyland-erupts-for-30-rams-throttle-aggies.aspx |website=Virginia Commonwealth University |access-date=December 12, 2020 |date=December 9, 2020}} Six days later, Hyland posted a career-high 31 points in a 93–68 victory over [[Western Carolina Catamounts men's basketball|Western Carolina]].{{cite web |title=Hyland scores 31 to lift VCU over Western Carolina 93–68 |url=https://www.si.com/college/college-basketball/game/2285367 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=December 18, 2020 |date=December 15, 2020}} On March 5, 2021, he recorded 30 points and 10 rebounds in a 73–68 win against [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] at the [[2021 Atlantic 10 men's basketball tournament|Atlantic 10 tournament]] quarterfinals.{{cite web |title=Hyland scores 30 to lift VCU past Dayton 73–68 in A-10 |url=https://apnews.com/article/basketball-hason-ward-jordy-tshimanga-jalen-crutcher-adrian-baldwin-5cc97c43b4cc29b71cabc9cb9ff8cae7 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=March 5, 2021}} As a sophomore, Hyland averaged 19.5 points, 4.7 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.9 steals per game, and was named [[Atlantic 10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic 10 Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Epps |first1=Wayne |title=VCU's Bones Hyland named Atlantic 10's player of year |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/vcus-bones-hyland-named-atlantic-10s-player-of-year/article_33d52e7a-ab0d-5de3-a09f-bcfe17d5ac2e.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=March 10, 2021}} On April 17, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Epps |first1=Wayne |title=VCU's Bones Hyland declares for NBA draft |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/vcus-bones-hyland-declares-for-nba-draft/article_88d5fd70-207e-5609-bfb9-136fc41874a8.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=April 17, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Denver Nuggets (2021–2023)=== On July 29, 2021, Hyland was drafted with the 26th overall pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]], becoming [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU's]] first draft pick in 11 years.{{cite news|last1=Singer|first1=Mike|date=July 31, 2021|title=Meet Nuggets draft pick Bones Hyland, VCU's "pied piper" and the pride of Wilmington|work=[[The Denver Post]]|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2021/07/31/bones-hyland-nuggets-draft-vcu-wilmington/|access-date=July 31, 2021}}{{Cite web|title=2021 NBA Draft results: Picks 1–60|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2021-nba-draft-results-picks-1-60|access-date=2021-08-01|website=NBA.com}} On January 15, 2022, Hyland scored a then career-high 27 points and had 10 rebounds in a 133–96 win against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite news |last1=Singer |first1=Mike |title=Bones Hyland, Nikola Jokic hammer LeBron James, Lakers in rout |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2022/01/15/bones-hyland-nikola-jokic-hammer-lebron-james-lakers-in-rout/ |access-date=January 16, 2022 |work=[[Denver Post]] |date=January 15, 2022}} On April 24, in the first round of the playoffs, Hyland helped the Nuggets to a 126–121 Game 4 victory over the [[Golden State Warriors]], with 15 points and 7 assists.{{cite web | title=Nuggets' Bones Hyland: Scores 15, sparks Game 4 victory | website=CBS Sports | date=2022-04-24 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nuggets-bones-hyland-scores-15-sparks-game-4-victory/ | access-date=2025-12-07}} Although Hyland played 42 games with the 2022-23 Nuggets and averaged more than 11 points per game before his trade, he was excluded from receiving a championship ring when Denver won the NBA title after sending him to the Clippers. ===Los Angeles Clippers (2023–2025)=== On February 9, 2023, Hyland was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in a four-team trade involving the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-acquire-hyland-from-denver-nuggets|title=LA Clippers Acquire Hyland from Denver Nuggets|work=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023}}{{Cite web |title=Magic Acquire Patrick Beverley, Future Second Round Draft Pick and Cash Considerations as Part of a Four-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-acquire-patrick-beverley-future-second-round-draft-pick-cash-considerations-four-team-trade-la-lakers-mo-bamba-release-20230209 |date=February 9, 2023 |website=NBA.com|quote=the L.A. Clippers acquire Bones Hyland from Denver}} On April 10, 2024, in a 124–108 loss against the [[Phoenix Suns]], Hyland scored a new career-high 37 points.{{cite web|author=Janis Carr|title=Bones Hyland, Clippers' reserves get a night to shine in loss to Suns|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2024/04/10/bones-hyland-clippers-reserves-get-a-night-to-shine-in-loss-to-suns/|website=dailynews.com|date=April 10, 2024|access-date=April 11, 2024}} === Minnesota Timberwolves (2025–present) === On February 6, 2025, Hyland and [[Terance Mann]] were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for guard [[Bogdan Bogdanović (basketball)|Bogdan Bogdanović]], and three second-round draft picks.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-receive-terance-mann-and-nahshon-bones-hyland-from-la-clippers|title=Atlanta Hawks Receive Terance Mann and Nah'Shon “Bones” Hyland from LA Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025}} He was waived the next day.{{Cite web |date=2025-02-08 |title=Hawks make 'red flag' final decision on former 1st-round pick |url=https://soaringdownsouth.com/hawks-hyland-trade-clippers-nuggets |access-date=2025-02-08 |website=Soaring Down South |language=en-us}} On February 27, Hyland signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web | agency=Associated Press | title=Wolves reward Jaylen Clark with new deal, sign Bones Hyland to 2-way contract | website=NBA.com | date=2025-02-28 | url=https://www.nba.com/news/timberwolves-sign-clark-hyland | access-date=2025-02-28}} In four appearances for Minnesota, he averaged 1.3 points, 0.3 rebounds, and 1.0 assist. On September 15, 2025, Hyland re-signed with the Timberwolves on a one-year minimum contract.{{Cite web |date=September 15, 2025 |title=Timberwolves Re-Sign Guard Bones Hyland |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-re-sign-guard-bones-hyland |access-date=November 1, 2025 |website=nba.com |language=en}} He would have a resurgence for the Timberwolves, becoming a key contributor off the bench, averaging 8.5 points and 2.6 assists in 16.6 minutes per game. On June 30, 2026, Hyland re-signed with the Timberwolves on another one-year minimum contract.{{Cite web |last=Maher |first=Rory |date=June 30, 2026 |title=Bones Hyland Re-Signs With Timberwolves On One-Year Deal |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2026/06/bones-hyland-re-signing-with-timberwolves-on-one-year-deal.html |access-date=July 4, 2026 |website=HoopsRumors.com}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2021}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2021–22 Denver Nuggets season|Denver]] | 69 || 4 || 19.0 || .403 || .366 || .856 || 2.7 || 2.8 || .6 || '''.3''' || 10.1 |- | style="text-align:left;" rowspan=2|{{nbay|2022}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2022–23 Denver Nuggets season|Denver]] | 42 || 1 || '''19.5''' || .399 || .378 || .866 || 2.0 || 3.0 || .7 || '''.3''' || '''12.1''' |- | style="text-align:left;"|[[2022–23 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
